text:
maria: FYI SFO-rtg-01 started showing sustained 95th pct streaming latency spikes around 21:03 UTC. Non-streaming (sync) throughput didn't drop but streaming responses started piling up in the runtime queue.
kevin: timeline? any capacity events or autoscale chatter?
maria: no autoscale events. GPU util stayed ~85% but queue depth jumped. Logs show a lot of `REQUEST_ACCEPTED` followed by `STREAM_PREEMPT_WAIT`. snippet: `2026-03-17T21:03:12Z INFO STREAM_PREEMPT_WAIT req=abcd shard=3`
sam: that suggests admission allowed sync/bulk to fill slots and streaming couldn't grab headroom. We're effectively starving the streaming fast-path.
kevin: are we still using the single global tokenpool per-shard? or did the dual buckets roll last month?
natalie: SFO is on the old config (global pool). We haven't rolled the per-mode token handshake to that fleet yet.
maria: customer-facing P95 went from 180ms -> 1.2s for streaming. Non-stream SLA fine. Ops alarm fired.
kevin: idea: introduce a lightweight "rate-handshake" during accept that returns an admission result + suggested delay / preemptible flag. example header: `X-Redwood-Admit: accept;mode=stream;budget=12ms;fallback=model-small`
sam: yeah — front proxy could use that to decide whether to switch to sync fallback or buffer client-side. It avoids blindly queuing stream requests into runtime when headroom missing.
natalie: implementation notes: runtime needs to atomically check per-shard budgets for streaming vs sync and return either `accept` or `defer` with an estimated backoff. We can reuse the existing admission counter but add a `preferred_mode` enum.
kevin: pseudo-config for proxy behavior: 
```
if admit.mode == stream and admit.status == defer:
  if client.prefers_low_latency: hold up to 200ms, then retry header-check
  else route to sync endpoint with `X-Redwood-Fallback: sync`
```
kevin: Also propose a tiny grace pool per-shard: 5% of tokens reserved for streaming short requests so they don't get fully starved by long-running sync jobs.
sam: agree, but watch cost: reserving tokens reduces gross throughput. We should make it tunable per-customer/tier.
maria: can telemetry show correlation between long sequence sync jobs and streaming p95 spikes? ops-telemetry-bot: @maria added a query to the dashboards: `top5 sync jobs by token-seconds vs streaming_p95` — results pinned to #infra-dash for 24h :mag: 
natalie: rollout plan: 1) enable admit headers in canary SFO shards 2) flip proxy handshake on canary prefix 3) enable grace pool 4) observe p95 and cost delta 5) roll region-wide.
kevin: testing tip: simulate mixed workload with `wrk2` harness and inject `mode=stream` long-poll vs short chat tests. script: `./tools/loadgen --streamers 200 --sync 50 --hold 2s`
sam: edge-case: what if proxy retries cause request duplication and increased KV cache pressure? need idempotency keys and retry-after headers.
maria: also check NLB timeouts — streaming clients may hold connections; if proxy defers, we need a 202+Retry-After semantic or websocket push to avoid client timeouts.
natalie: I'll draft admission response schema: {"status": "accept|defer|fallback", "mode": "stream|sync", "budget_ms": int, "fallback_hint": string} and expose as headers + small json body when necessary.
kevin: do we want immediate preemption (evict sync slot to give streaming its token) or soft-defer? immediate preempt increases tail of the evicted sync request. I'd prefer soft-defer first.
sam: agree. soft-defer + short grace pool, then observe. If still bad, evaluate preemption policy that only kicks in for critical customers.
maria: any blockers for canary?
natalie: infra: need a small runtime patch (admission API + metrics), proxy change, and dashboard queries. I can land runtime change in a small PR, then deploy to canary.
kevin: i'll prep the proxy PR. include metric `admit.deferred.count` and `admit.budget.ms.hist`
maria: action items: 
- natalie: runtime admit API PR and grace-pool flag (due EOD tomorrow)
- kevin: proxy handshake & retry/backoff behavior PR (due +2d)
- sam: loadtest script + baseline numbers (due +1d)
- ops-telemetry-bot: pin dashboard and alert tweak for streaming-p95 > 500ms

maria: thanks all. tagging customer success to notify impacted tenant. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deploy for `runtime/admit-v1` to SFO-rtg-01 at 2026-03-18T03:30:00Z (ETA 3m).
ops-telemetry-bot: Dashboard updated, chart `SFO streaming p95 vs sync token-seconds` now under Infra > Canary.
kevin: leaving notes in PR for rollback thresholds and SLAs.
maria: will monitor after canary. if p95 drops we roll fast.
